playArea.grid: Same grid as heightmap.png: pixel (col, row) is centered on heightmap vertex (col, row), i.e. x = (col - 800) * 5, z = (row - 800) * 5. Row 0 = -z (grid north), column 0 = -x. The image covers x, z in [-4002.5, 4002.5] m.
playArea.uv: u = (x + 4002.5) / 8005, v_down = (z + 4002.5) / 8005 (v_down = 0 at the top row). With the default three.js PlaneGeometry spanning -4000..4000 the error is at most half a texel (2.5 m).
playArea.values: linear_albedo = srgb_to_linear(value / 255). Mean of real pixels and of filled pixels = 0.22 (value 129). Load as a color map with colorSpace = SRGBColorSpace; to use it as a multiplier on another base color, divide the decoded linear value by 0.22.
playArea.filled: 20.0% of pixels (permanent and cast shadows, no data, grazing light) carry texture copied from nearby lit ground (mean = neutral), feathered over ~2 pixels.

source.dataset: LROC NAC de Gerlache Rim low-Sun controlled mosaic, combined mosaic #1, 5 m/px version (NAC_ROI_DEGERRIMLO1_P885S2933_5M); 144 NAC images from 2009-2013, 3 Sun-azimuth bins
source.citation: Henriksen, M.R., Burnette, S.R., Brown, H.M., Wagner, R.V., Robinson, M.S., Collins, W.M., Grieser, S.A., Boyd, A.K. (2023), Optimized Illuminated Terrain Coverage of the Candidate Artemis III Landing Sites with LROC NAC Controlled Mosaics, European Lunar Symposium, pp. 134-135
source.license: PDS archive product, public domain (credit NASA/GSFC/Arizona State University)
source.shadingDem: LOLA Site11 5 m DEM (Barker et al. 2021), same grid as heightmap.png

processing: Cropped on the native 5 m grid (it is pixel-aligned with Site11 / heightmap.png; no resampling).

Alignment check: correlation of the image with the DEM shading model, shifting the DEM by up to 3 pixels; see 'alignment'. A best shift of 0 or 1 pixel (5 m) means the texture lines up with heightmap.png within the source's stated 5-20 m accuracy; no shift is applied.

Fill: shadows (darker than 25% of the 300 m local mean), no data and pixels where the model predicts under 15% of flat-ground light, dilated by two pixels, are filled by copying real texture from lit ground 185 m to 1.7 km away (fixed offsets, nearest first), so holes are not flat; their mean is still neutral.

Shading removal: local Lambert fit I ~ g * (n . s) with n from the DEM, solved per pixel by Gaussian-weighted least squares (sigma 150 m), because the mosaic mixes images with three Sun azimuths. Fitted Sun azimuth (from grid north toward +X) p10/p50/p90 = [31.0, 204.0, 222.0] deg; apparent elevation p10/p50/p90 = [6.9, 13.3, 22.8] deg (the images list incidence 86-91 deg, i.e. the Sun -1..4 deg above the mean surface; the fit is only a local shading model, and the 5 m DEM is smoother than the real surface).
Albedo = image / fitted shading, clipped to 0.25..3.0, i.e. albedo relative to the ~150 m neighbourhood.
limits: Large-scale (> ~300 m) brightness differences are removed on purpose: in this mosaic they are mostly exposure and Sun-angle differences between images, not albedo.
Craters and boulders smaller than the DEM resolves (< ~20 m) keep their baked bright/dark crescents from the original Sun direction.

Shadowed areas (permanent shadows and shadows at imaging time) carry no image data; their texture is copied from nearby lit ground, so it is plausible but not real. ShadowCam mosaics could fill them in a later pass.
No color: the NAC is a single broadband (panchromatic) channel.
